decisions.friction_cancellation_shortcut: Not admitted: net remainder opposes normal impulse before yaw5 in20/20 records. It includes commanded traction, not an identified exogenous disturbance to cancel.
decisions.reference_only_cause: Still rejected by8 no-clamp yaw failures; endpoint local effects remain open.
decisions.strict_zero_unloading_as_primary: Not adopted:8/16 original successes have some central zero upward-target-normal samples. This is not proof of flight; original scores unchanged.
decisions.next_candidate: Impact-phase common/differential wheel coordination, with existing bounds and published delayed39 packet only. Candidate mechanism, not novel or qualified algorithm yet.

candidate.hypothesis: Adding controlled common wheel authority alongside unchanged differential wheel authority may reduce early impact yaw response while retaining original speed/arrival/height/roll/physics/design gates.
predictions: With same Nom and actuator limits, additional common wheel action lowers initial normal-moment impulse and yaw peak without using lateral obstacle avoidance as full-passage evidence.
Benefits must survive all original task gates and strong-classical comparison; reducing yaw while harming roll/high-height/speed/arrival/stop/height rejects candidate.
Authority question requires matched policy/training/information treatment and same-information nonlearning common braking reference; frozen V6 channel masking cannot identify matched-learning effect.
candidate.information: Same published39 packet, same delay/cadence and original ideal fast Nom in all arms; new contact forces/COM/true trajectory/geometry only evaluation, never policy/controller privilege.
candidate.distinctiveness: Common/differential actions and basic braking are standard engineering; no novelty claim.174 must check closest work, feasibility/authority and distinguish a defensible method before registering any learning budget.
candidate.falsification: No common-authority benefit, lost strong-classical successes, any physical/design deterioration, or no defensible methodological distinction closes this candidate. No added budget/gain tuning to rescue it.

limitations: Observational decomposition, not counterfactual effect or angular-momentum balance. Outcome-defined contact-to-yaw5 window is exploratory, not a preregistered treatment metric. Remainder includes feedback traction/torsional/rolling effects; impulse does not directly prove yaw acceleration. Figure is a declared illustrative0.16m case, not aggregate benefit.
